chunks: From him, from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The wife is returned (due to defects) for four things: leprosy, leprosy-like disease (al-Judham), madness, and blindness (al-Qaran), which is al-Afal (complete blindness). If these have not occurred upon her, she is returned; if they have occurred upon her, she is not returned. The reasoning in these two narrations is also what we said: that when he marries her with knowledge of her condition, he does not have the right to return her, because that is his consent, which indicates acceptance of the defect.
ai.seo_question: What are the four defects in a wife that allow for her return in Shia Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani’s al-Istibsar details the four specific defects—leprosy, leprosy-like disease, madness, and blindness—that grant a husband the right of *khiyar al-uyub* (option of defect) in Shia jurisprudence. It clarifies that this right is contingent upon the defect being present at the time of marriage; if the husband marries with prior knowledge of the condition, his consent is presumed, and he forfeits the right to return her. This ruling underscores the principle of transparency in marital contracts, ensuring that defects known to the spouse do not constitute grounds for annulment.
